# Draft:Conquest of Dąbrów (1410)

The Conquest of Dąbrów - the battle of the Polish-Lithuanian army against the Teutonic State at Dąbrówno (German: Gilgenburg), fought on 13 July 1410.
Battle
The Polish-Lithuanian army, in order to march towards the north as planned, had to cross the road and capture this town.In the Chronicle of the Conflict by an unknown author, it is written that King Jagiello ordered the city to be captured by ‘good people’. Jan Długosz, on the other hand, in his Books of the Famous Kingdom of Poland, claims that this happened without the king's order. The battle began in the evening of 13 July 1410 and lasted three hours. We know its detailed course thanks to the description in Długosz's book.Jacek Bednarek: Zamek krzyżacki w Dąbrównie. Zamkipolskie.pl. [dostęp 2025-02-16]. (pol.).
Długosz wrote that the day after the battle, on 14 July, Jagiełło stayed in burnt Dąbrówno to collect the spoils and food buried in pits and cellars and to take care of the captives captured in the town. He detained brother-knights, noblemen and landowners and released all townsmen, country folk and women, regardless of condition and age. In addition, he recommended a guard over them to ensure that none of the knights released from captivity did any harm. In the evening, the king announced the march for the following day and ordered the knights to rest so that they would be ready to set off before dawn. On 15 July 1410, the Battle of Grunwald took place.Jacek Bednarek: Zamek krzyżacki w Dąbrównie. Zamkipolskie.pl. [dostęp 2025-02-16]. (pol.).
